concepts.def: Identifying what a performer does well and less well, the starting point of any performance evaluation.
Judging performance against an elite or 'perfect' model to pinpoint differences and areas to improve.
Analysing whether weaknesses are technical, tactical, physical or psychological in origin.
Practices, drills and coaching methods chosen to address the identified weaknesses.
A structured, progressive plan setting out how and when improvements will be made and reviewed.
Approaches such as feedback, demonstration and guidance used to help a performer improve.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Evaluating and Analysing Performance for Improvement (EAPI) — a core area of A-Level PE.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Evaluating and Analysing Performance for Improvement (EAPI) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Evaluating and Analysing Performance for Improvement (EAPI).

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: In EAPI, what is the usual first step?
options: Identifying strengths and weaknesses in performance
Designing the team kit
Booking a stadium
Choosing a diet only

options: Pinpoint differences and areas to improve

Financial
